text: The new j-piece is the sum of Pᵢ over degree(i)=j. Grouping each finite decomposition gives spanning, and projection onto each fiber recovers its component, establishing the bijectivity in [Mathlib’s internal-sum definition](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean#L440). Any index map is allowed; empty fibers give the zero submodule. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/TensorProduct.lean#L141) passes.
Actual total-degree application groups tensor bidegrees p,q with p+q=n.

Writing a kernel element as a finite sum from the spanning Aᵢ gives a zero sum of images in the independent A′ᵢ. Each image vanishes by [Mathlib’s finite-sum independence criterion](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/DFinsupp.lean#L581), giving ker(g)=Σᵢ(ker(g)∩Aᵢ). Source independence is unnecessary; the target independence and ring hypotheses are explicit. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/Mixed/Substructure.lean#L206) passes.
Actual application to the rational kernel via the complex Deligne splitting.

Injectivity of f transfers uniqueness of components; hproj lifts every component of f(x), and hmem puts its preimage in the prescribed summand. Thus recomposition is bijective as required by [Mathlib’s internal-sum definition](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean#L440). This generalizes the component-stable submodule criterion in [Hazrat §1.2.2](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=21) to injective maps over semirings. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Quotient.lean#L115) passes.
Actual homogeneous-submodule application preserves the ambient components.
The induced summand has exactly ambient degree membership.

The equivalence E agrees on each generator with the inclusion after eᵢ. Direct-sum extensionality therefore identifies canonical recomposition with E composed with the inverse component equivalences. It is bijective, exactly [Mathlib’s internal-sum definition](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean#L440); the displayed generator-compatibility hypothesis is essential. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/DirectSum.lean#L192) passes.
Actual application constructs the internal degree decomposition of an external direct sum.

The value is the range of [Mathlib’s componentwise map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L249) applied to subtype inclusions. Range membership is equivalent to xᵢ∈Nᵢ for every i because the ambient x already has finite support. It therefore describes precisely the direct sum of these submodules inside the ambient direct sum. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/DirectSum/Internal.lean#L125) passes.
The range is exactly the componentwise membership submodule.
A single allowed component belongs to that range.

A zero relation between the image summands lifts to a sum lying in ker(f)∩ΣAᵢ. The kernel hypothesis decomposes it within ker(f)∩Aᵢ; source independence identifies the components, so each image vanishes by [Mathlib’s finite-sum independence criterion](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/DFinsupp.lean#L581). The ring assumption supports subtraction and is retained. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Quotient.lean#L209) passes.
Actual homogeneous quotient application preserves canonical components.
Quotient pieces are precisely the images of the original pieces.

For x∈p, hp places every canonical component in p∩Aᵢ, and the finite reconstruction sums to x. The reverse inclusion follows from p being a submodule. This is the spanning equality in [Hazrat §1.2.2](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=21)’s graded-submodule criterion, valid here for semirings and arbitrary index sets. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/Weights/Multiplicity.lean#L54) passes.
Actual application decomposes a component-stable weight space and adds its finite dimensions.

The equation is f(πᵢx)=πσ(i)(f(x)): expand x into homogeneous terms and use injectivity of σ to exclude contributions from other indices. This extends [Hazrat §1.2.3](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=22)’s degree-shifting map convention to arbitrary additive subobjects. The additive map f itself need not be injective. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Internal.lean#L351) passes.
Degree-r maps specialize σ to i↦i+r.
A possibly noninjective quotient map commutes with degree-zero projection.

The ambient generator at i is the image of the corresponding generator with value x∈Nᵢ. That gives its range-membership witness for piSubmodule. This is the single-component calculation of [Mathlib’s componentwise map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L249); every other component is zero and belongs to its designated submodule. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/DirectSum/Internal.lean#L79) passes.
The explicit preimage maps to the asserted ambient generator.

This is [Mathlib’s componentwise map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L249) applied to the subtype maps Nᵢ→Mᵢ. It sends each finitely supported family to the same coordinates in the ambient modules, preserving addition and scalars. Subtype injectivity gives an inclusion for any index family, including an empty one. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/DirectSum/Internal.lean#L71) passes.
The i-th coordinate is the underlying original component.
The map preserves insertion at a single index.

Both internal decompositions are supplied, and hmem makes f preserve their corresponding summands. Uniqueness of target components gives f(πᵢx)=πᵢ(f(x)), the degree-zero case of [Hazrat §1.2.3](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=22). This statement needs no injectivity of f; it also computes the projections in the injective restriction construction. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Quotient.lean#L115) passes.
The actual subtype inclusion recovers ambient homogeneous projection.

Included families have each coordinate in Nᵢ. Conversely, componentwise membership lifts an ambient finitely supported family to ⨁Nᵢ, with no new support. Thus the equivalence is the subtype specialization of [Mathlib’s range formula](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L292). The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/DirectSum/Internal.lean#L113) passes.
The inverse range equivalence retains exactly the ambient coordinates.

Applying [Mathlib’s componentwise map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L249) to an inserted component changes only its codomain through the subtype inclusion. Hence both sides have value x at i and zero elsewhere. DecidableEq supplies this insertion, and the dependent family Mᵢ remains the same on both sides. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/DirectSum/Internal.lean#L71) passes.
The coordinate formula determines the generator equality.
The generator equation supplies its range-membership witness.

The componentwise subtype map is injective, so LinearEquiv.ofInjective identifies ⨁Nᵢ with its range piSubmodule N. This uses [Mathlib’s componentwise map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L249) and its injectivity criterion. The inverse returns the same coordinates with membership proofs; finite support is inherited from the ambient family. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/DirectSum/Internal.lean#L103) passes.
The forward equivalence is precisely the inclusion.
The inverse restores every ambient coordinate.

LinearEquiv.ofInjective uses the original inclusion as its forward function. Forgetting the range-membership proof therefore yields exactly piInclusion N x, with the coordinates prescribed by [Mathlib’s componentwise map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L249). This is an equality in the ambient direct sum for every finitely supported x. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/DirectSum/Internal.lean#L71) passes.
The underlying inclusion has precisely the original coordinates.

The object is the ordinary algebra quotient H/I with the descended Hopf structure from [Mathlib’s Hopf quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/HopfAlgebra/Quotient.lean#L37). The ring hypotheses and Hopf-ideal laws suffice; no flatness is needed. Published [zero-quotient](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L381) and [augmentation-quotient](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Augmentation.lean#L57) controls pass. The construction does not take the radical of I or claim an fppf quotient of groups.
Zero quotient is identified by the lift of the identity.
Augmentation quotient comparison composes its projection with the scalar isomorphism to the counit.

This bundles the canonical map h↦[h] as a commutative Hopf-algebra morphism, as in [Mathlib’s Hopf quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/HopfAlgebra/Quotient.lean#L37). Published [evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L120) and [surjectivity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L146) controls pass. Its direction is H→H/I; on represented affine groups the direction reverses. Neither a section nor an inverse is asserted.
Projection evaluates as the ordinary quotient class.
Every quotient element has a representative.

Forgetting the categorical wrapper gives the original quotient bialgebra morphism from [Mathlib’s Hopf quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/HopfAlgebra/Quotient.lean#L37). Hence the scalar, comultiplication and counit structures remain those of the canonical projection. The published [underlying-linear-map control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L126) passes. This equality does not introduce a separately chosen projection or an inverse to the quotient.
The underlying R-linear map is the same ideal quotient projection.

The morphism evaluates to the standard quotient class, consistent with [Mathlib’s Hopf quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/HopfAlgebra/Quotient.lean#L37). Both sides use the same ideal I.toIdeal and land in H/I. The published [vanishing control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L139) passes, detecting exactly the elements of I. No representative of an arbitrary quotient element is selected.
Vanishing of a quotient class is exactly membership in I.

The underlying R-linear map is the ordinary ideal quotient map, matching the scalar quotient in [Mathlib’s Hopf quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/HopfAlgebra/Quotient.lean#L37). The published [pointwise control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L120) passes and determines this equality by linear extensionality. This is equality of maps H→H/I, not an identification of H/I with a chosen complementary submodule of H.
Projection evaluates as the ordinary quotient class.

The ordinary ring-hom kernel of h↦[h] is precisely I.toIdeal, the quotient convention underlying [Mathlib’s kernel quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). The published [nested-ideal control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L447) passes and preserves the direction I≤J. This theorem identifies an ordinary ideal kernel and does not require the separate flat-kernel constructor.
For I≤J, the quotient by J kills I.

A quotient class vanishes exactly when its representative lies in I, the zero-fiber calculation behind [Mathlib’s kernel quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). The published [kernel equality](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L133) passes. The right side is membership in the original Hopf ideal, not its radical; this matters for nonreduced quotients as well as for I=0.
The ordinary kernel of the quotient morphism is I.toIdeal.

Every quotient element has a representative in H, so the canonical projection is onto, as used by [Mathlib’s Hopf quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/HopfAlgebra/Quotient.lean#L37). The published [categorical-epimorphism control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L152) passes. Surjectivity is about the coordinate-algebra function H→H/I, not a statement about the induced map on spectra or on algebra-valued group points.
Surjective quotient projection is an actual categorical Epi proposition.

Surjectivity of the underlying quotient map makes it right-cancellable among Hopf-algebra morphisms, the uniqueness part of [Milne, Proposition 3.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). The published [cancellation control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L158) passes. The instance establishes Epi for this specific projection; it does not assert that every categorical epimorphism is surjective.
Precomposition with the quotient projection detects equality of outgoing morphisms.

Maps H/I→X agreeing after the projection agree on every quotient class, matching the uniqueness in [Milne, Proposition 3.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). The published [quotient-lift uniqueness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L196) control passes. The hypothesis compares precompositions q≫f and q≫g; cancelling a map on the wrong side or assuming q injective is unnecessary.
The factor with the specified composite is the unique quotient lift.

The hypothesis I≤ker f makes [h]↦f(h) well-defined, and the original bialgebra laws descend as in [Milne, Proposition 3.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). Published [representative evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L180) and [uniqueness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L196) controls pass. No surjectivity of f is needed for this forward factorization, and the codomain remains K.
The induced map sends [h] to f(h).
The factor with the specified composite is the unique quotient lift.

Forgetting the categorical wrapper yields the same bialgebra quotient lift used in [Milne, Proposition 3.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). The published [factorization control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L187) passes using this identity. Both sides retain the same ideal-killing hypothesis and preserve comultiplication and counit, not merely the underlying ring map.
Projection then quotient lift equals the original map.

The lift evaluates on the class of h as f(h), the explicit map in [Milne, Proposition 3.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). Vanishing on I makes this independent of representative. The published [nested-quotient evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L472) control passes, sending [h] modulo I to [h] modulo J when I≤J. The formula chooses no inverse representative.
Nested-quotient map sends [h] modulo I to [h] modulo J.

Projection followed by the lift equals f, the factorization identity of [Milne, Proposition 3.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). The published [nested-quotient composition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L523) control passes. Equality is of Hopf-algebra morphisms H→K; the categorical order q≫f̄ correctly means applying q first and the lift second.
Successive quotienting along I≤J agrees with quotienting by J.

Given k∈K, surjectivity of f supplies h with f(h)=k, and the quotient lift sends [h] to k by [Milne, Proposition 3.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). The published [nested-quotient control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L481) passes. The explicit hsurj hypothesis is necessary; merely killing I does not imply that an arbitrary quotient lift is onto K.
Nested-quotient map is onto under the stated containment.

Equality I=J identifies the two quotient objects and their canonical projections, consistently with the quotient object in [Mathlib’s Hopf quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/HopfAlgebra/Quotient.lean#L37). The displayed transport runs from H/J to H/I using the reversed equality. The published [ideal-matching transport control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L323) passes. Only proof-level equality transport occurs; no new algebra automorphism is chosen.
Explicit ideal-matching equality transport preserves the forward quotient square.

The surjective composite H→K→K/I has kernel f⁻¹(I), so its first-isomorphism map gives H/f⁻¹(I)≅K/I, as in [Mathlib’s kernel quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). Published [class evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L245) and [quotient compatibility](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L231) controls pass. The forward map is [h]↦[f(h)]; ring-level surjectivity supplies the Hopf kernel without flatness.
Surjective quotient transport sends [h] to [f(h)].
The surjective transport square commutes as Hopf-algebra morphisms.

Both paths send h to [f(h)] in K/I, matching the first-isomorphism forward map of [Mathlib’s kernel quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). The published [pointwise class control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L245) passes. The source quotient is by f⁻¹(I), so the square has matching types; the ideal equality transport does not alter the map on representatives.
Surjective quotient transport sends [h] to [f(h)].

An ambient isomorphism is surjective, so the first-isomorphism construction underlying [Mathlib’s kernel quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35) identifies H/e⁻¹(I) with K/I. Published [forward](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L263) and [inverse](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L272) compatibility controls pass. The source ideal is the preimage under e.hom; no ideal invariance is required unless source and target ideals are to be identified.
Ambient isomorphism gives the forward commuting quotient square.
Inverse quotient isomorphism gives the matching square with e.inv.

The induced quotient map sends [h] to [e(h)], so quotienting before or after e gives the same result, as in [Mathlib’s kernel quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). The published [inverse-square control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L272) passes. Both sides start at H and end at K/I, with the source quotient formed from e⁻¹(I).
Inverse quotient isomorphism gives the matching square with e.inv.

The definition is the continuous R-linear dual of C(X,R), with values in E. For compact p-adic X and scalar coefficients this is Colmez’s measure notion. The type synonym deliberately adds no topology on measures; no positivity or countable-additive set function is asserted. Compared with [the reference](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~pierre.colmez/fonctionsdunevariable.pdf#page=31) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/Basic.lean#L40).

This is the identity linear equivalence from the measure type synonym to its continuous-functional carrier. Evaluation is unchanged in both directions. It expresses the defining dual description of a measure, without asserting an isometry or equivalence between weak and norm topologies. Compared with [the reference](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~pierre.colmez/fonctionsdunevariable.pdf#page=31) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/Basic.lean#L84).

Addition and negation are inherited pointwise from continuous linear functionals. The topological additive-group hypothesis on E preserves continuity under these operations. This gives the usual additive structure on the dual description of p-adic measures, with no positivity restriction. Compared with [the reference](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~pierre.colmez/fonctionsdunevariable.pdf#page=31) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/Basic.lean#L62).

The scalar action is pointwise multiplication of functional values by R-scalars. Commutativity of R preserves R-linearity, and ContinuousSMul preserves continuity. This is the standard module structure on the continuous dual, generalized from scalar-valued p-adic measures to E-valued functionals. Compared with [the reference](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~pierre.colmez/fonctionsdunevariable.pdf#page=31) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/Basic.lean#L78).

The usual p-adic integer ring is compact for its norm topology. The proof combines completeness with finite residue representatives modulo pᵏ giving arbitrarily fine finite covers. It agrees with Breuning’s compactness statement and uses primality explicitly. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/math5020f11/breuningnotes.pdf#page=11) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/ProperSpace.lean#L58).

The forward difference is f(x+h)−f(x), with this sign and no division by h. At h=1 it is the operator used for Colmez’s Mahler coefficients. Constants are killed; iteration zero is the identity. The definition works on an additive monoid domain. Compared with [the reference](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~pierre.colmez/fonctionsdunevariable.pdf#page=8) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/ForwardDiff.lean#L40).

Iterated forward differences commute with a fixed scalar action because that action distributes over subtraction. The result holds for a distributive monoid action, including natural-number scalars. It supplies the coefficient linearity in the Mahler transform without requiring division or scalar inverses. Compared with [the reference](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~pierre.colmez/fonctionsdunevariable.pdf#page=8) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/ForwardDiff.lean#L121).

A summation filter is exactly a filter on finite subsets, allowing the same partial-sum construction to express unconditional or ordered summation. NeBot and eventual inclusion of each index are separate conditions, so the definition correctly retains filters that need not give unique or nonvacuous sums. Compared with [the reference](https://us.metamath.org/mpeuni/df-tsms.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/InfiniteSum/SummationFilter.lean#L32).

The unconditional summation filter is atTop on finite subsets ordered by inclusion. Thus every fixed finite set is eventually included, independently of any enumeration. Its NeBot instance prevents vacuous convergence, including for empty or finite index types. Compared with [the reference](https://us.metamath.org/mpeuni/df-tsms.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/InfiniteSum/SummationFilter.lean#L170).

The class requires every represented function to be continuous and tend to the specified zero outside compact sets. It is the polymorphic version of C₀’s defining condition. It makes no claim that F contains every such function, so subclasses and additional bundled structure are allowed. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/mpugh/Teaching/Mat1000/Mar_26_03.pdf#page=15) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty.lean#L64).

Pointwise products preserve continuity and decay to zero, and the sup seminorm satisfies ‖fg‖≤‖f‖‖g‖. The nonunital conclusion is appropriate on arbitrary domains: a constant identity need not vanish at infinity. No norm separation or completeness is asserted. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/mpugh/Teaching/Mat1000/Mar_26_03.pdf#page=15) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty.lean#L485).

The bound has constant one: ‖r•x‖≤‖r‖‖x‖. It follows from IsBoundedSMul’s metric estimate and preservation of zero. This matches the contractive scalar inequality in JN’s normed modules, while the stated algebraic assumptions allow more general actions. Compared with [the reference](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1604.07739#page=8) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/MulAction.lean#L34).

An ultrametric sum has norm at most any nonnegative common bound for its terms. For summable families this is the finite-sum bound passed to the limit, as in Conrad’s estimate. Without summability, tsum is zero by convention; the theorem does not infer convergence. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/gradnumthy/infseriespadic.pdf#page=1) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Ultra.lean#L334).

Evaluation cannot exceed the uniform seminorm of a bounded continuous function. This is the defining supremum bound, with no compactness requirement and no assumption that the supremum is attained. The source reduces it to the corresponding uniform-distance estimate. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/math5020f11/breuningnotes.pdf#page=14) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/Bounded/Normed.lean#L63).

For C≥0, a uniform seminorm bound is equivalent to the bound at every point. The nonnegativity premise is essential when the domain is empty: the pointwise condition is then vacuous while the function seminorm is zero. This is the standard sup-norm characterization. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/math5020f11/breuningnotes.pdf#page=14) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/Bounded/Normed.lean#L88).

A nonnegative pointwise bound controls the ℓ∞ norm, including for dependent families of normed groups. The proof uses the supremum property for nonempty indices and handles the empty index type separately. This is the expected bounded-sequence estimate. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/math5020f11/breuningnotes.pdf#page=14) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Lp/lpSpace.lean#L628).

Each coordinate is bounded by the ℓp size for every p≠0, including p=∞ and 0<p<1. For finite p the proof compares one nonnegative pth-power term with the whole sum; infinity uses the supremum. No triangle inequality for p<1 is asserted. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~hunter/measure_theory/measure_notes.pdf#page=83) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Lp/lpSpace.lean#L600).

The structure bundles a σ-semilinear map and continuity of its underlying function. The ordinary notation takes σ to be the identity, recovering continuous linear maps. It does not infer boundedness from continuity over arbitrary topological modules; that equivalence requires extra hypotheses. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/math5020f11/breuningnotes.pdf#page=13) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L60).

The fields encode zero preservation, subadditivity and symmetry under negation. Nonnegativity follows from 0=s(x−x)≤2s(x), so its absence as a separate field is correct. This matches Temkin’s additive-group seminorm on abelian groups and extends it to arbitrary additive groups. Compared with [the reference](https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Introduction_to_Berkovich_Spaces.pdf#page=4) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Seminorm.lean#L61).

A real bound tending to zero forces a seminorm-bounded function to tend to zero in the seminorm topology. Indeed 0≤‖f‖≤a squeezes the real norms to zero. This applies to arbitrary filters and does not require separation, completeness or a linear structure. Compared with [the reference](https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Introduction_to_Berkovich_Spaces.pdf#page=4) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Continuity.lean#L103).

The discrete factor indexes open sheets, and the equation for the first coordinate makes the homeomorphism commute with f. Openness of the preimage is explicit because continuity of f is not assumed initially. The empty index type correctly describes an empty preimage neighborhood. Compared with [§1.3 p.56, evenly covered neighborhood definition](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L39).

Every base point has a projection-compatible local product with its actual discrete fiber. This implies continuity and allows empty fibers, exactly as the source documentation and Hatcher specify. No single global sheet count or surjectivity is part of the definition. Compared with [§1.3 p.56, including the explicit empty-sheet convention](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L287).

Separatedness here concerns distinct points with the same image. The local product places them in distinct discrete sheets, giving disjoint open neighborhoods in E. This is exactly the local-sheet consequence used in covering lift uniqueness; it does not assert that all of E is Hausdorff. Compared with [§1.3 p.56 and Proposition 1.34 proof, p.62](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L348).

Two continuous lifts of the same function agree everywhere on a preconnected domain once they agree at the supplied point a. The point argument provides nonemptiness, so PreconnectedSpace gives precisely the connected-domain uniqueness statement. Local path-connectedness is unnecessary. Compared with [Proposition 1.34, p.62](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L367).

A continuous map from a preconnected space whose composite with f is constant has constant image in E. Its image lies in one discrete fiber; the two supplied arguments make the conclusion pointwise. Empty domains cause no unsupported choice of a constant value. Compared with [p.60, constancy of lifts into a discrete fiber; connected-domain consequence](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L371).

The structure combines the quotient topology and surjectivity, fibers equal to G-orbits, continuous individual group translations, and a neighborhood disjoint from every nonidentity translate. Translating both sets gives Hatcher’s pairwise-disjoint condition. No topology on G is required: the formulation is for a discrete group action. Compared with [§1.3 p.72, condition (*) and orbit-space construction](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Quotient.lean#L36).

The conclusion is freeness: g • e = g′ • e forces g = g′. Applying the disjoint-neighborhood hypothesis to g′⁻¹g and the point e gives that cancellation. This is stronger than injectivity of each individual translation and requires no additional separation hypothesis. Compared with [§1.3 pp.72–73, condition (*) implies freeness](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Quotient.lean#L75).

The quotient and disjoint-translate conditions produce evenly covered neighborhoods of every base point. The source passes to the interior of the chosen neighborhood and constructs a local trivialization; quotient surjectivity supplies a point over each x. No local path-connectedness or Hausdorffness is needed. Compared with [Proposition 1.40(a), p.72](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Quotient.lean#L222).

Any continuous lift Γ of γ with Γ(0)=e computes the monodromy endpoint as Γ(1). The exact statement compares underlying points of E; projection already places that endpoint in the required final fiber. No separate terminal-point assumption is needed. Compared with [§3.2 p.22, unique path lifting; §3.3 p.23, fiber translation](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Lifting.lean#L398).

An upstairs path class from ex to ey whose projected class is γ proves monodromy(γ,ex)=ey. The casts align the fiber-membership endpoint equalities. Equality of classes suffices because monodromy is invariant under homotopy fixing both endpoints. Compared with [§3.2(ii) p.22 and §3.3 p.23](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Lifting.lean#L430).

Path.trans traverses γ first and γ′ second, so transport first applies monodromy γ and then monodromy γ′. The fiber types line up x→y→z, and the source reduces the formula to concatenation of lifted paths. This is covariant composition in traversal order. Compared with [§3.3 p.23, fiber translation functor](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Lifting.lean#L440).

The action sends a loop class and an initial fiber point to the lifted endpoint. FundamentalGroup.mul_def traverses the right factor first, so monodromy gives a left MulAction. This agrees with May’s multiplication convention; copying Hatcher’s left-to-right convention without inversion would change the formula. Compared with [§1.2 p.6 and §3.3 p.23](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Lifting.lean#L447).

This is the permutation representation induced by the preceding left action on the fiber. Reversing a loop gives inverse transport, while the multiplication law uses Mathlib’s right-to-left loop product. The codomain is the permutation group of this fiber, not the deck-transformation group. Compared with [§1.2 p.6; §3.3 p.23, invertibility of fiber translation](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Lifting.lean#L454).

Forgetting the permutation structure returns exactly the forward endpoint-transport function on the loop class γ.asHom. There is no inverse loop hidden in this coercion. The exact extracted type confirms equality of functions on the fiber, rather than equality with a deck transformation. Compared with [§3.3 p.23, fiber translation function](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Lifting.lean#L458).

The functor assigns each point its fiber and each fixed-endpoint path class its lifted-endpoint map. Identity and composition are the actual monodromy laws, so the functor is covariant into Type. This matches the docstring’s monodromy definition and May’s fiber translation functor without requiring connectedness. Compared with [§3.3 p.23, fiber translation functor](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf); [In point-set topology, Definition: monodromy of a covering space (docstring cites Definition 2.1)](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/monodromy) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Lifting.lean#L464).

The generated map equation exposes the functor’s arrow as TypeCat.ofHom applied to forward monodromy of f. The extracted morphism has exactly the initial and final fibers as domain and codomain. The generator’s actual map field verifies this equation and excludes an accidental contravariant or inverse transport. Compared with [§3.3 p.23, arrow formula for fiber translation](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf); [In point-set topology, monodromy definition](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/monodromy) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Lifting.lean#L464).

Transport along a path class is a bijection between its two endpoint fibers. The inverse comes from the reversed class; the source equivalently uses that a functor from a groupoid sends every arrow to an isomorphism. It does not equate arbitrary fibers lying in different path components. Compared with [§3.3 p.23, inverse translation along the inverse arrow](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Lifting.lean#L470).

The homomorphism takes value g in Gᵐᵒᵖ exactly when g.unop sends the chosen fiber point e to its monodromy endpoint. Freeness makes that group element unique. This is the endpoint-coordinate characterization of the source definition, with no commutativity or simple-connectivity hypothesis. Compared with [§1.3 pp.73–74, group element identified by a lifted endpoint](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf); [§1.2 p.6, multiplication convention](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Lifting.lean#L651).

Unwrapping the opposite-group value and acting on e recovers exactly the lifted endpoint. This verifies the selected group coordinate in E, including its direction. Changing e can conjugate that coordinate; the formula itself needs neither an abelian group nor a simply connected total space. Compared with [§1.3 pp.73–74, lifted-endpoint identification](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf); [§1.2 p.6, multiplication convention](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Lifting.lean#L670).

For a simply connected total space, endpoint coordinates give a multiplicative equivalence π₁(X,x)≃Gᵐᵒᵖ. Source surjectivity uses paths from e to g•e, and injectivity uses trivial lifted-loop classes. Local path-connectedness is correctly absent, as in Hatcher Exercise 28. The opposite group is required by Mathlib’s loop order and the commuting left G-action. Compared with [§1.3 Exercise 28, p.82; compare Proposition 1.40(c), p.72](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf); [§1.2 p.6, right-to-left loop multiplication](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Lifting.lean#L728).
